eligibility.quote: The same occurs if the command is split into two separate calls, one stopping the old and one starting the new controller.
eligibility.reason: E1/E4: #343 supplies a reproducer and resource-claim rejection, corroborated by #345. E2: separately instantiated controller plugins compete for exclusive command interfaces retained across deactivation. E3: SWITCH is directly reproduced even with separate stop/start calls. Host-framework implementation of the fix does not make the resource interaction deployment wiring or a build issue.

failed_conditions.quote: [controller_manager]: Resource conflict for controller 'forward_position_controller2'. Command interface 'joint1/position' is already claimed.
failed_conditions.reason: The log proves the exclusive claim conflict on joint1/position. Both joint1/position and joint2/position are implicated because the reproducer copies the same two-joint position controller configuration; the first reported rejection need not enumerate all retained resources.

detection_stage.reason: The new controller cannot claim interfaces when it is activated after the old controller is stopped.

resolution.quote: it matches perfectly with what I patched locally on the repo
resolution.reason: This confirms agreement with the patch, not a successful revision-identified run of the two forward controllers. The inspected fix adds release_interfaces after deactivate and supplies tests using different controller fixtures, supporting recommended.

notes: The separate discussion of simultaneously starting two controllers returning success concerns a CONCURRENT operation, not this SWITCH composition. It is therefore not added as a missed condition. The host controller_manager revision is material to reproducing the switch even though the selected two controller units are unchanged by the fix.
